roots.name: Ingredient Bubbles Around Product
roots.mechanism: ingredient transparency — 'look how much goodness is inside'
roots.why_it_works: Each floating sphere is a proof point; the ring of ingredients around a single product makes a multi-herb formula feel generous and premium without a word of claim.
roots.visual_motif: Product centered and upright; translucent spheres arranged in a ring around it, one raw ingredient per sphere, each with a small label; soft radial glow; price/CTA badge in a corner.
roots.compliance_notes: Sphere labels must be ingredient names only, never 'X treats/controls Y'. If a benefit is shown per ingredient, use the approved Rule 4 phrasing ('Arjuna Chhal - supports healthy lipid levels'). No disease words on labels. Disclaimer if any benefit text appears.

roots.name: Botanical Habitat / Forest Floor
roots.mechanism: naturalness & provenance — the product belongs in nature
roots.why_it_works: Placing the product in a lush natural scene with its raw ingredients scattered around it makes 'plant-based / ayurvedic' feel literal and unprocessed; the eye reads 'this came from the earth'.
roots.visual_motif: Product resting on a mossy forest floor or among foliage; raw herbs/roots arranged naturally around the base; ingredient names floating with thin callout lines; diffused daylight; earthy green-brown palette.
roots.compliance_notes: Floating labels = ingredient names only. Any headline stays Type A (broad wellness) or Type C (ingredient-led). No 'for PCOS / diabetes / cholesterol' framing like the competitor uses.

our_executions.note: Box in a forest, herbs scattered, Hindi labels around

roots.name: Pile vs One (VS Comparison)
roots.mechanism: simplification + loss-aversion — 'stop juggling many, switch to one'
roots.why_it_works: A hand overflowing with many pills/bottles next to a hand holding one product dramatizes effort and cost; the contrast does the persuading, no claim needed.
roots.visual_motif: Split frame or two hands: left = messy pile of generic pills / many supplement bottles; right = one clean hand holding our single product; short 'why take X when...' headline; per-day price badge.
roots.compliance_notes: Headline stays Type B question ('15 alag-alag cheezein kyun lein...'). Do not claim our one product replaces the medical function of the pile. Comparison is about count/convenience/cost, not efficacy.
